== Biography ==

The Dormouse is a creature distinguished by his pronounced somnolence. He is present at the Mad Tea-Party held beneath a tree, where he sits between the March Hare and the Hatter, settling immediately into sleep. The two companions show little regard for his comfort, using him as a cushion and resting their elbows upon him as they converse over his head. Extraordinarily, despite his sleeping state, the Dormouse participates in the philosophical absurdities of the tea party. Speaking from within his slumber, he contributes paradoxes of his own—remarking that breathing while one sleeps is equivalent to sleeping while one breathes.

The Dormouse later appears at the trial of the Knave of Hearts, attending with the March Hare and the Hatter. He offers testimony during the proceedings, declaring "Sixteenth" when dates are discussed. Seated near Alice during the trial, he protests as she grows larger in the crowded courtroom, imploring her: "I wish you wouldn't squeeze so. I can hardly breathe."

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. The Dormouse appears at the tea party alongside Alice and later sits beside her during the trial, where he complains of being squeezed.

'''[[March Hare]]''' — acquaintance. The Dormouse is intimately positioned between the March Hare and the Hatter at the tea party, and enters the courtroom arm-in-arm with the March Hare at the trial.

'''[[Hatter]]''' — acquaintance. The Dormouse participates with the Hatter in the tea party's absurd logical exchanges and later accompanies him to the trial.

'''[[Queen]]''' — adversary. The Queen reacts with fury to the Dormouse's singing, reportedly declaring him "murderous" toward time and calling for his death.

''Evolution:''
